Join Our Mission-Driven Team

Retirement Housing Foundation (RHF) is seeking an experienced Director of Operations (West Region)
to provide strategic leadership and operational oversight for a portfolio of affordable housing communities throughout the western United States.

As a key member of the Operations leadership team, you will lead Regional Managers, drive operational excellence, strengthen compliance efforts, improve financial performance, and support organizational growth initiatives. This is an exciting opportunity to join a mission-driven organization dedicated to providing quality affordable housing and services that help people thrive.

If you are a collaborative leader with extensive affordable housing experience and a passion for developing teams, improving operations, and making a meaningful impact, we encourage you to apply.

What You'll Do

Leadership & Team Development

Lead, coach, mentor, and develop Regional Managers.
Establish performance expectations and accountability measures.
Support succession planning, employee engagement, and workforce development initiatives.
Partner with Human Resources on recruiting, onboarding, and employee development efforts.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Operations Management

Oversee day-to-day operations of affordable housing communities throughout the assigned region.
Drive occupancy, resident satisfaction, operational efficiency, and service excellence.
Identify operational challenges and implement effective solutions.
Promote consistency in policies, procedures, and best practices across the portfolio.
Utilize reporting and data analysis to improve operational performance.

Financial Oversight

Review financial statements, budgets, occupancy trends, and key performance indicators.
Monitor operating results and support expense management initiatives.
Partner with Regional Managers to improve asset performance and address operational challenges.
Assist with budget preparation, financial forecasting, and strategic planning.

Compliance & Risk Management

Ensure compliance with HUD, LIHTC, Tax Credit, and other affordable housing regulations.
Provide guidance during audits, inspections, management reviews, and compliance assessments.
Monitor regulatory changes and implement operational adjustments as needed.
Support risk management and asset preservation initiatives.

Strategic Leadership

Support acquisitions, property transitions, new developments, and growth initiatives.
Collaborate with executive leadership to achieve organizational objectives.
Provide operational analysis, recommendations, and performance updates.
Represent RHF with governmental agencies, boards, ownership groups, and community stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Real Estate, Property Management, or a related field.
Minimum seven (7) years of progressively responsible property management experience, including oversight of multi-site housing portfolios.
Minimum three (3) years of management experience leading managers or senior-level staff.
Experience managing HUD, LIHTC, Tax Credit, and/or Conventional Housing communities.
Strong knowledge of affordable housing regulations and property management operations.
Strong financial, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Exceptional leadership, communication, and relationship-building abilities.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and property management software systems such as Yardi.
Valid California driver's license and insurable driving record.
Ability to travel throughout the assigned region, including occasional overnight travel.

Preferred Qualifications

Certified Property Manager (CPM).
Housing Credit Certified Professional (HCCP), COS, TCS, or similar affordable housing certification.
Experience overseeing large, geographically dispersed portfolios.
Experience with acquisitions, portfolio transitions, growth initiatives, and operational integration projects.
Nonprofit housing experience.

Why Join RHF?

For more than 60 years, RHF has been committed to providing affordable housing and services that enhance the lives of older adults, low-income families, and persons with disabilities. Our employees play a critical role in fulfilling that mission every day. As Director of Operations, you will have the opportunity to help shape organizational strategy, support employee growth, strengthen communities, and make a positive difference in the lives of thousands of residents.

Competitive compensation
Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
Generous Paid Time Off and Holidays
Retirement Savings Plan
Life Insurance
Employee Assistance Program
Professional Development Opportunities
Collaborative and Mission-Driven Culture

RHF prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind and makes all employment decisions based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Program Overview

Community Solutions, Inc. is seeking a dedicated a passionate candidate to fill the role of Program Director for our Multi-Dimensional Anti-Recidivism Partnership (MAP) located in Barstow, CA and Victorville, CA. The selected candidate will be leading and managing the daily operations of the program through recruiting, training, and providing supervision and development to staff members, while ensuring that the program is operating in a manner that exemplifies CSI's values, including principles of diversity, equity and inclusion. MAP is an innovative program dedicated to engaging the community and providing rehabilitative programming for justice-involved individuals. We focus on promoting long-term, self-sustaining skills through vocational training and personal development services. This unique model hosts a variety of sub-contractors at one site to reduce barriers for clients.

Position Overview

Review and approve all staff duties and client paperwork including but not limited to, program plans, monthly progress reports, closing summaries, and counseling forms.
Conduct, with the assistance of any supervisory staff, recruitment for all program positions.
Conduct and facilitate staff orientation and training using in-service and outside agency resources.
Ensure supervised staff receive a minimum of required hours of training annually.
Monitor program and staff compliance with all agency policy and procedure.
Ensure compliance with other relevant criteria including referring agency requirements and applicable standards.
Perform policy and program audits as required.
Evaluate program effectiveness and cost-efficiency.
Review weekly sanitation and safety inspection reports and address deficiencies.
Monitor on an ongoing basis program expense and revenue budget categories.
Maintain monthly documentation on above and justify variations from budget averages targeted.
Develop annual program budget and establish fiscal priorities.
Ensure proper accountability over program resources including food, utilities, telephone, and house and office supplies.
Approve and coordinate client referrals and intakes from respective contracting agencies.
Identify, coordinate and monitor existing and new outside agency resources for program and agency use.
Develop contacts with outside agencies and individuals which may foster agency and program growth.
Perform the functions of Human Service Worker or Case Manager that relate to client supervision, treatment and custody as needed.
Directly investigate and handle all client appeals of a disciplinary or grievance nature.
Coordinate and participate in all client admissions, orientation, and removals.
The Program Director should be ready to perform any tasks, reasonably assigned, that are needed to maintain the viability of the Program.

Annual Salary: $102,622.30

Qualifications

Qualifications:

A Master's degree and three years of experience, or a Bachelor's degree and five years of experience in the social service or criminal justice field. Education may be substituted with relevant experience on a one-year-for-one-year basis.
Three years of experience in management and supervision of staff.
Ability to engage and develop collaborations with community agencies.
Previous assessment and experience with Microsoft Office preferred.

Benefits

Generous Time Off:
2 weeks of vacation for first year (increasing to 3 weeks after 1 year), 7 days of sick time, and 4 floating holidays.

Health & Wellness:
Medical, dental, and voluntary vision plans, plus FSA, short-term disability, accident insurance, hospital coverage, life insurance, and AD&D options.

401(k) Retirement Plan:
Automatic enrollment with a 100% company match up to 4%.

Professional Development:
Tuition reimbursement after 1 year, plus ongoing training and opportunities for certification.

Annual Salary:
The salary range for this position starts at $85,000 and the offer will be reflective of experience, education, skillset, etc.

Company Overview

Community Solutions Inc. (CSI) is a nonprofit organization that promotes the responsible citizenship, accountability, and well-being of individuals and families involved, or at risk of involvement, in the child welfare, juvenile justice, or criminal justice system. Since CSIs founding in 1962, it has been a pioneer in the community-based service. We have been delivering supervision, treatment, and comprehensive individualized services to help clients interact more effectively in their communities and become productive citizens. Using this plan, we built the first ever halfway house in New England which has now been replicated and grown to almost 50 programs in 9 states. For over 50 years, CSI has been building upon its successful foundations and has been expanding its services to serve thousands of adults, youth, and families each year.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Gift Planning
jobs.description:
Posting Summary

TC's Office of Institutional Advancement seeks an experienced frontline fundraiser to serve as Executive Director of Gift Planning. The Executive Director of Gift Planning will be entrusted with advancing the College’s long-term philanthropic goals and strengthening its culture of legacy giving by providing strategic leadership for the institution’s gift planning program.

Job Summary/Basic Functions

The Executive Director is responsible for the development, growth, and management of a comprehensive gift planning program. This role engages alumni, parents, friends, and other constituents in a donor-centric way to making the largest gift possible through estate and blended gift commitments (including bequest intentions, beneficiary designations, life income plans such as charitable gift annuities and charitable remainder trusts); in support of the institution’s mission, students, faculty, and academic priorities. The Executive Director reports to the Assistant Vice President of Leadership Giving and supervises an Assistant Director, Planned Giving. Key responsibilities include:

Frontline Fundraising
Engage prospects and donors in meaningful conversations about ways to support TC in the future by managing a portfolio of approximately 50-75 prospects with six- and seven-figure giving capacity. Qualify donors; develop cultivation strategies and plans to optimize donor’s tax position and maximize their interest in supporting TC; and ensure appropriate gift agreements are in place to document bequest intentions.
Assist donors with bequest intentions, beneficiary designations, life income plans such as charitable gift annuities and charitable remainder trusts, and complex asset gifts.
Partner with the Donor Relations and Stewardship team to ensure that all donors within the officer’s portfolio are stewarded appropriately as individuals and through the Grace Dodge Society membership.
Travel as needed to meet with prospective and current donors.

Strategy & Program Leadership
Develop and execute a comprehensive planned giving strategy aligned with Teachers College priorities in coordination with the AVP of Leadership Giving and the VP for Institutional Advancement.
Serve as the College’s senior expert on planned giving and estate gifts, including bequest intentions, beneficiary designations, life income plans such as charitable gift annuities and charitable remainder trusts, and complex asset gifts.
Collaborate closely with colleagues to support a culture of planned giving across Institutional Advancement, including providing frontline guidance on structuring gifts that include planned gift vehicles and partnering with alumni relations, annual giving, stewardship, and communications teams to embed planned giving messaging throughout the donor lifecycle.
Management of the Grace Dodge Society, including increasing visibility through effective marketing, communications, and partnership with Donor Relations on an annual Grace Dodge Society signature event.
Oversee Planned Giving marketing and communications efforts, including interfacing with outside vendors.
Manage an Assistant Director, Planned Giving.

Administrative
Partner with the Assistant Vice President of Operations on all administrative and compliance matters related to administration of realized planned gifts, ensuring compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and institutional gift acceptance policies.
Oversee, working with the Assistant Director of Planned Giving, the College’s efforts to report to New York State authorities on our life income gifts, including coordinating as needed with State Street Global Advisors to ensure timely and accurate transactions and annual reporting relating to gift annuities and charitable trusts.
Ensure timely and accurate record keeping of all outreach, donor activity, and proposals in Raiser’s Edge, TC's database of record for all donor information.
Collaborate as needed with colleagues on the development of gift planning proposals and gift agreements.
Identify and attend professional development opportunities to stay current in the field of gift planning.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or the equivalent of education and experience required
Minimum of 8–10 years of experience in planned giving, major gifts, or related advancement roles
Deep knowledge of estate planning, tax considerations, and charitable gift vehicles
Ability to translate complex financial and legal concepts into accessible language for donors and campus partners
Demonstrated success securing planned gifts and blended gifts
Strategic and analytical thinking with a long-term, institutional perspective
High level of discretion, integrity, and professionalism
Ability to navigate complex academic environments and multiple stakeholders
Experience working with fundraising databases
Experience managing staff and leading collaborative, cross-functional initiatives
Ability to travel regularly for donor visits and alumni events, including occasional evening and weekend commitments
Strong organizational and planning skills

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree and/or professional credentials such as JD, CPA, CFP
Experience with Raiser’s Edge and Salesforce
Experience in higher education preferred

Salary Range

$155,000 - $175,000 annually

Work Modality

Hybrid

Competitive Compensation And Benefits

The salary range reflects the College’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the compensation for the position at the time of the job posting. Salary decisions are dependent on several factors including but not limited to market and organizational considerations, experience, and qualifications of a selected candidate as well as internal and external equity.

Our benefits contribute significantly to the total compensation package that includes medical, dental, vision, and supplemental insurance plans; flexible and hybrid work schedules; tuition remission; life insurance; short and long-term disability insurance; an exceptional employer retirement matching program; health savings accounts (HSA), flexible spending accounts (FSA), Public Service Loan Forgiveness eligibility, and a robust Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

Hybrid/Remote

Teachers College maintains a hybrid work environment, which provides employees with flexible work arrangements while ensuring we preserve the important aspects of our unique in-person college-campus culture. Depending on role and business needs, colleagues will either work onsite or in a hybrid model (a combination of in-office and virtual days). Employees are expected to live within a 150-mile radius of the College.

Job Description

CEO/General Manager

Gem City Market – Dayton, Ohio

Retained Search Partner: The Carlisle Group

Salary Range: $90,000 – $115,000

The Carlisle Group is pleased to be partnered on a retained search with Gem City Market
in Dayton, Ohio, in the search for their next CEO/General Manager
.

Gem City Market is a community-centered, full-service grocery cooperative created to bring quality, affordable food to a diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood in Dayton. More than simply a grocery store, Gem City Market is committed to being a pillar of the community it serves—helping strengthen the local culture, creating opportunity, and providing a welcoming place where neighbors can shop, connect, and thrive.

The co-op is seeking an entrepreneurial, community-minded grocery leader who can balance mission and margin
—someone who understands that a successful cooperative must deliver both meaningful community impact and strong financial performance. The CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to lead the Market into its next chapter while ensuring that customers receive quality products at affordable prices in a clean, welcoming, and inclusive environment.

Living in Dayton

Dayton offers an appealing combination of affordability, accessibility, community, and opportunity
. Located in southwest Ohio, Dayton provides the amenities of a larger metropolitan area while retaining a strong sense of neighborhood and community.

The city has a rich history of innovation, entrepreneurship, and community involvement and is home to a diverse collection of neighborhoods, restaurants, arts and cultural attractions, parks, and outdoor recreation. Residents enjoy access to an extensive regional park system, the great Miami River, biking and hiking trails, and numerous opportunities to enjoy the outdoors.

Dayton's location is another advantage. Cincinnati and Columbus are both within approximately an hour's drive, while Cleveland and Indianapolis are accessible within a few hours. The region offers a relatively affordable cost of living compared with many larger U.S. metropolitan areas, making Dayton an attractive place to build both a career and a life.

For a leader who wants to make a tangible difference in a community while enjoying a high quality of life, Dayton presents a compelling opportunity.

Position Purpose

The CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading Gem City Market as a successful, financially sustainable cooperative while advancing the goals and purposes established by the Board of Directors.

The CEO/General Manager Will Ensure That The Market

Operates efficiently and ultimately profitably.
Provides quality, affordable groceries that meet the needs of its customers.
Maintains a clean, welcoming, and inclusive shopping environment.
Builds a positive culture for employees and the broader community.
Advances the cooperative's mission and role as a community institution.
Remains responsive to the needs of the diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood it serves.

The CEO/General Manager will bring together the disciplines of grocery operations, financial management, merchandising, people leadership, marketing, and community engagement
to ensure the continued success of Gem City Market.

Overview Of Responsibilities

Operations

Lead an efficient, customer-focused, and ultimately profitable cooperative grocery operation.
Create a positive store atmosphere and build a motivated, accountable staff team.
Maintain current knowledge of grocery retailing, industry trends, and best practices, particularly those applicable to cooperative markets and urban, low- to moderate-income communities.
Develop and maintain productive relationships with market partners, wholesale distributors, local markets, and other industry resources.
Establish and maintain an appropriate product mix that meets shopper needs while supporting financial objectives.
Develop and execute a margin strategy that allows Gem City Market to remain price competitive while maintaining adequate cash flow.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, licenses, permits, health requirements, and employment standards.
Continuously evaluate operational performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, customer service, and profitability.

Financial Management & Strategic Planning

Develop and recommend long- and short-range plans designed to achieve the cooperative's purposes and strategic objectives.
Direct the financial operations of the cooperative and maintain accountability for the organization's financial performance.
Develop operating, capital, and cash budgets for Board approval and manage the business within approved financial parameters.
Provide regular, meaningful financial and operational reporting to the Board of Directors.
Monitor key grocery industry metrics and use financial and operational data to make informed decisions.
Identify new business opportunities and make recommendations to the Board regarding potential growth, partnerships, and innovation.
Participate in regional and national cooperative and grocery industry events to remain connected to emerging trends and best practices.

People & Culture

Determine the appropriate staffing structure and maintain clear, effective job descriptions.
Hire management personnel and oversee the hiring, training, development, and retention of Market staff.
Create a positive, productive, inclusive, and accountable workplace culture.
Manage and evaluate employees while providing timely coaching, feedback, recognition, and accountability.
Establish appropriate compensation structures based upon the budget, local labor market, and competitive conditions.
Organize staffing to promote a fair distribution of work while maintaining excellent customer service.
Develop and maintain an effective employee benefits program.
Build a culture where employees understand the Market's mission and their role in delivering it.

Marketing & Community Engagement

Develop and execute an effective advertising and marketing strategy that maintains strong public awareness of Gem City Market and its products and services.
Ensure marketing activities are executed within established budgetary guidelines.
Communicate effectively with cooperative members, customers, employees, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Prepare or oversee the preparation of the annual report and other communications to the cooperative's members and community.
Ensure that store displays, signage, promotions, and merchandising effectively support sales and customer engagement.
Strengthen Gem City Market's position as a trusted and visible community institution.
Identify opportunities to deepen relationships with local organizations, businesses, producers, and community partners.

Reporting Relationships

The CEO/General Manager reports directly to the Board of Directors
, which includes Market staff and members of the community.

The Board is responsible for establishing the organization's overall direction, goals, and expectations, while the CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading day-to-day operations and executing the strategy established by the Board.

The CEO/General Manager has the authority to hire, direct, structure, develop, and evaluate all other Market staff.

The successful candidate will understand the importance of building a strong, collaborative relationship with the Board based on trust, transparency, accountability, and open communication
.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will bring a combination of grocery retail expertise, financial acumen, leadership ability, entrepreneurial thinking, and a genuine commitment to community.

Grocery Retail Leadership

Minimum of five years of successful experience managing a retail grocery store.
Strong understanding of grocery store operations and the various departments required to achieve sales, margin, labor, and profitability goals.
Demonstrated understanding of key grocery industry metrics and how to use them to drive performance.
Experience managing both retail and administrative functions.
Knowledge of current grocery industry trends and competitive dynamics.
Experience with merchandising and marketing in highly competitive grocery markets.

Financial Management

Demonstrated bottom-line accountability for a grocery or retail operation.
Strong understanding of financial variables and their relationship to overall business performance.
Experience developing and managing operating, capital, and cash budgets.
Ability to analyze financial and operational information and translate it into effective business decisions.
Demonstrated ability to balance affordability and customer needs with margin, cash flow, and profitability requirements.

Leadership & People Management

Proven ability to motivate, lead, and coordinate people to achieve organizational objectives.
Experience hiring, training, evaluating, developing, compensating, and, when necessary, terminating employees.
Ability to establish clear expectations and hold people accountable.
Strong listening skills and the ability to both give and receive constructive feedback.
Self-aware, self-motivated, and comfortable taking ownership of decisions and outcomes.
Ability to handle multiple priorities and demands while maintaining focus on the organization's most important objectives.

Cooperative & Community Leadership

Genuine understanding of and appreciation for the cooperative business model.
Ability to articulate what makes a cooperative different and how cooperative principles influence decision-making.
Experience working effectively with a Board of Directors.
Ability to build trust with Board members, employees, customers, and community stakeholders.
Service-oriented leadership style with a genuine interest in improving the community served by the organization.
Experience working in a food desert, food-insecure, or low-income community is highly valued.

Strategic & Entrepreneurial Thinking

Ability to make difficult decisions and take appropriate risks when necessary.
Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify root causes and develop practical solutions.
Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to recognize and pursue opportunities for innovation and growth.
Ability to maintain momentum and lead change with a sense of urgency.
Willingness to seek outside expertise and perspectives when appropriate.
Ability to balance immediate operational demands with the long-term health and sustainability of the cooperative.

The Opportunity

This is a unique opportunity for a hands-on grocery leader and community-minded executive
to lead an organization with a purpose that extends well beyond the four walls of a grocery store.

The next CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to strengthen Gem City Market's financial and operational performance while helping fulfill its larger role as a source of affordable food, employment, connection, and opportunity within the Dayton community.

For the right leader, this is more than an opportunity to run a grocery store. It is an opportunity to help build a stronger community through grocery retail.

Interested candidates should contact Brett Myers, Managing Director of The Carlisle Group
, for more information regarding this retained search at bcm@tcgrecruit.com
.

Job Description

CEO/General Manager

Gem City Market – Dayton, Ohio

Retained Search Partner: The Carlisle Group

Salary Range: $90,000 – $115,000

The Carlisle Group is pleased to be partnered on a retained search with Gem City Market
in Dayton, Ohio, in the search for their next CEO/General Manager
.

Gem City Market is a community-centered, full-service grocery cooperative created to bring quality, affordable food to a diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood in Dayton. More than simply a grocery store, Gem City Market is committed to being a pillar of the community it serves—helping strengthen the local culture, creating opportunity, and providing a welcoming place where neighbors can shop, connect, and thrive.

The co-op is seeking an entrepreneurial, community-minded grocery leader who can balance mission and margin
—someone who understands that a successful cooperative must deliver both meaningful community impact and strong financial performance. The CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to lead the Market into its next chapter while ensuring that customers receive quality products at affordable prices in a clean, welcoming, and inclusive environment.

Living in Dayton

Dayton offers an appealing combination of affordability, accessibility, community, and opportunity
. Located in southwest Ohio, Dayton provides the amenities of a larger metropolitan area while retaining a strong sense of neighborhood and community.

The city has a rich history of innovation, entrepreneurship, and community involvement and is home to a diverse collection of neighborhoods, restaurants, arts and cultural attractions, parks, and outdoor recreation. Residents enjoy access to an extensive regional park system, the great Miami River, biking and hiking trails, and numerous opportunities to enjoy the outdoors.

Dayton's location is another advantage. Cincinnati and Columbus are both within approximately an hour's drive, while Cleveland and Indianapolis are accessible within a few hours. The region offers a relatively affordable cost of living compared with many larger U.S. metropolitan areas, making Dayton an attractive place to build both a career and a life.

For a leader who wants to make a tangible difference in a community while enjoying a high quality of life, Dayton presents a compelling opportunity.

Position Purpose

The CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading Gem City Market as a successful, financially sustainable cooperative while advancing the goals and purposes established by the Board of Directors.

The CEO/General Manager Will Ensure That The Market

Operates efficiently and ultimately profitably.
Provides quality, affordable groceries that meet the needs of its customers.
Maintains a clean, welcoming, and inclusive shopping environment.
Builds a positive culture for employees and the broader community.
Advances the cooperative's mission and role as a community institution.
Remains responsive to the needs of the diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood it serves.

The CEO/General Manager will bring together the disciplines of grocery operations, financial management, merchandising, people leadership, marketing, and community engagement
to ensure the continued success of Gem City Market.

Overview Of Responsibilities

Operations

Lead an efficient, customer-focused, and ultimately profitable cooperative grocery operation.
Create a positive store atmosphere and build a motivated, accountable staff team.
Maintain current knowledge of grocery retailing, industry trends, and best practices, particularly those applicable to cooperative markets and urban, low- to moderate-income communities.
Develop and maintain productive relationships with market partners, wholesale distributors, local markets, and other industry resources.
Establish and maintain an appropriate product mix that meets shopper needs while supporting financial objectives.
Develop and execute a margin strategy that allows Gem City Market to remain price competitive while maintaining adequate cash flow.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, licenses, permits, health requirements, and employment standards.
Continuously evaluate operational performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, customer service, and profitability.

Financial Management & Strategic Planning

Develop and recommend long- and short-range plans designed to achieve the cooperative's purposes and strategic objectives.
Direct the financial operations of the cooperative and maintain accountability for the organization's financial performance.
Develop operating, capital, and cash budgets for Board approval and manage the business within approved financial parameters.
Provide regular, meaningful financial and operational reporting to the Board of Directors.
Monitor key grocery industry metrics and use financial and operational data to make informed decisions.
Identify new business opportunities and make recommendations to the Board regarding potential growth, partnerships, and innovation.
Participate in regional and national cooperative and grocery industry events to remain connected to emerging trends and best practices.

People & Culture

Determine the appropriate staffing structure and maintain clear, effective job descriptions.
Hire management personnel and oversee the hiring, training, development, and retention of Market staff.
Create a positive, productive, inclusive, and accountable workplace culture.
Manage and evaluate employees while providing timely coaching, feedback, recognition, and accountability.
Establish appropriate compensation structures based upon the budget, local labor market, and competitive conditions.
Organize staffing to promote a fair distribution of work while maintaining excellent customer service.
Develop and maintain an effective employee benefits program.
Build a culture where employees understand the Market's mission and their role in delivering it.

Marketing & Community Engagement

Develop and execute an effective advertising and marketing strategy that maintains strong public awareness of Gem City Market and its products and services.
Ensure marketing activities are executed within established budgetary guidelines.
Communicate effectively with cooperative members, customers, employees, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Prepare or oversee the preparation of the annual report and other communications to the cooperative's members and community.
Ensure that store displays, signage, promotions, and merchandising effectively support sales and customer engagement.
Strengthen Gem City Market's position as a trusted and visible community institution.
Identify opportunities to deepen relationships with local organizations, businesses, producers, and community partners.

Reporting Relationships

The CEO/General Manager reports directly to the Board of Directors
, which includes Market staff and members of the community.

The Board is responsible for establishing the organization's overall direction, goals, and expectations, while the CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading day-to-day operations and executing the strategy established by the Board.

The CEO/General Manager has the authority to hire, direct, structure, develop, and evaluate all other Market staff.

The successful candidate will understand the importance of building a strong, collaborative relationship with the Board based on trust, transparency, accountability, and open communication
.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will bring a combination of grocery retail expertise, financial acumen, leadership ability, entrepreneurial thinking, and a genuine commitment to community.

Grocery Retail Leadership

Minimum of five years of successful experience managing a retail grocery store.
Strong understanding of grocery store operations and the various departments required to achieve sales, margin, labor, and profitability goals.
Demonstrated understanding of key grocery industry metrics and how to use them to drive performance.
Experience managing both retail and administrative functions.
Knowledge of current grocery industry trends and competitive dynamics.
Experience with merchandising and marketing in highly competitive grocery markets.

Financial Management

Demonstrated bottom-line accountability for a grocery or retail operation.
Strong understanding of financial variables and their relationship to overall business performance.
Experience developing and managing operating, capital, and cash budgets.
Ability to analyze financial and operational information and translate it into effective business decisions.
Demonstrated ability to balance affordability and customer needs with margin, cash flow, and profitability requirements.

Leadership & People Management

Proven ability to motivate, lead, and coordinate people to achieve organizational objectives.
Experience hiring, training, evaluating, developing, compensating, and, when necessary, terminating employees.
Ability to establish clear expectations and hold people accountable.
Strong listening skills and the ability to both give and receive constructive feedback.
Self-aware, self-motivated, and comfortable taking ownership of decisions and outcomes.
Ability to handle multiple priorities and demands while maintaining focus on the organization's most important objectives.

Cooperative & Community Leadership

Genuine understanding of and appreciation for the cooperative business model.
Ability to articulate what makes a cooperative different and how cooperative principles influence decision-making.
Experience working effectively with a Board of Directors.
Ability to build trust with Board members, employees, customers, and community stakeholders.
Service-oriented leadership style with a genuine interest in improving the community served by the organization.
Experience working in a food desert, food-insecure, or low-income community is highly valued.

Strategic & Entrepreneurial Thinking

Ability to make difficult decisions and take appropriate risks when necessary.
Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify root causes and develop practical solutions.
Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to recognize and pursue opportunities for innovation and growth.
Ability to maintain momentum and lead change with a sense of urgency.
Willingness to seek outside expertise and perspectives when appropriate.
Ability to balance immediate operational demands with the long-term health and sustainability of the cooperative.

The Opportunity

This is a unique opportunity for a hands-on grocery leader and community-minded executive
to lead an organization with a purpose that extends well beyond the four walls of a grocery store.

The next CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to strengthen Gem City Market's financial and operational performance while helping fulfill its larger role as a source of affordable food, employment, connection, and opportunity within the Dayton community.

For the right leader, this is more than an opportunity to run a grocery store. It is an opportunity to help build a stronger community through grocery retail.

Girl Talk Development Director Job Description 

        Girl Talk, Inc. – Knoxville, TN 

Girl Talk, Inc. is a nonprofit organization that empowers girls to become their best selves through reducing the likelihood of teenage pregnancy and increasing the likelihood of educational advancement.

Position Summary

Girl Talk, Inc. is seeking a strategic, relationship-driven Development Director to lead the organization’s fundraising, donor relations, and development efforts. Reporting to the Executive Director, the Development Director is responsible for developing and executing fundraising strategies that strengthen donor relationships, diversify revenue, and generate sustainable funding to support Girl Talk’s mission, operations, and growth.

This position requires a strong relationship builder who can think strategically, execute effectively, and take ownership of fundraising goals and results.

Essential Responsibilities

Develop and execute Girl Talk’s annual development and fundraising plan.
Establish and meet annual fundraising goals in partnership with the Executive Director.
Identify, cultivate, solicit, steward, and retain individual, corporate, and foundation donors.
Build and maintain an active pipeline of prospective donors and funding opportunities.
Develop strategies to increase donor retention, engagement, and giving.
Maintain consistent communication and relationships with current and prospective donors.
Create fundraising appeals, sponsorship materials, donor communications, newsletters, and solicitation materials.
Research funding opportunities, write grant proposals, and ensure timely submission of grant reports and renewals.
Manage donor records and fundraising activity within the organization’s CRM.
Lead fundraising strategy, sponsorships, donor engagement, and planning for the annual Girl Talk Gala.
Coordinate donor cultivation, appreciation, and fundraising events.
Develop and implement social media and marketing strategies that support fundraising, donor engagement, and organizational visibility.
Track and regularly report fundraising activity, donor pipeline, revenue secured, and progress toward annual goals.
Collaborate with the Executive Director, Board, and staff on donor cultivation, solicitations, and organizational funding priorities.
Stay informed of fundraising trends and opportunities within the nonprofit and philanthropic community.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Fundraising Performance Expectations

The Development Director is accountable for generating sustainable contributed revenue and demonstrating a measurable return on Girl Talk’s investment in the position.
Within the first 12–18 months, the Development Director is expected to generate and/or retain contributed revenue equal to at least the fully loaded annual cost of the position. Thereafter, the position is expected to generate revenue exceeding its annual cost and contribute meaningfully toward Girl Talk’s annual fundraising and growth goals.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business Administration, Communications, Nonprofit Management, or related field preferred.
5+ years of fundraising, development, donor relations, or related nonprofit experience preferred.
Demonstrated experience cultivating donors and generating contributed revenue.
Grant writing experience.
Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
Ability to think strategically and effectively execute a plan.
Strong initiative, creativity, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Highly organized with excellent attention to detail and follow-through.
